pickleball.11six24-vapor-alpha-pro-power: A soft, forgiving hybrid with Power series pop. The catch: barely more power than the cheaper original.
pickleball.gearbox-gbx-power-elongated: An elongated paddle with easy power. The catch: a stiff feel makes soft shots harder to place.
pickleball.bread-butter-filth-hybrid: A comfortable, stable all-court hybrid. The catch: power is solid but not top tier.
pickleball.diadem-warrior-blucore: A soft, dampened foam paddle with easy touch. The catch: limited pop and spin at a premium price.
pickleball.crbn4-trufoam-waves: A hybrid much like the Genesis with a bit more punch. The catch: a small sweet spot that drops off fast.
pickleball.crbn1-trufoam-waves: A long-reach elongated with precise, spinny hits. The catch: a tight sweet spot with dead zones off center.
pickleball.gearbox-pro-ultimate-power-elongated-14m: A plush, high-swing-weight elongated with top-tier pop. The catch: a small sweet spot and a weak soft game.
pickleball.holbrook-fuze-vantagrit: A soft, dense all-court paddle with heavy spin. The catch: grit durability is unproven.
pickleball.joola-hyperion-cas: A lighter, balanced elongated with soft touch and a gritty face. The catch: the grit wears faster than the CFS.
pickleball.luzz-cannon-xpp-m1: A spin-heavy, head-heavy elongated with real power. The catch: heavy hands at the net.
pickleball.joola-perseus-power-fx: A stiff, hollow, poppy foam paddle with a rough face. The catch: little dwell for dinks and drops.
pickleball.neonic-flare-prime-x: A light, poppy widebody with quick hands and a low price. The catch: a stiff feel can make drops harder to place.
pickleball.paddletek-the-reserve-honeyfoam: A plush, dwelling foam paddle for dinks and spin. The catch: low power at a $250 price.
pickleball.prokennex-black-ace-pro: A light paddle with big power. The catch: a small sweet spot that punishes off-center hits.
pickleball.ronbus-beta-ripple-r2-14: A very light widebody with top-tier power and a big sweet spot. The catch: it needs added weight to settle down.
pickleball.ronbus-ripple-v2-r1-14: A head-heavy elongated power paddle with big plow-through. The catch: slow hands at the net.
pickleball.rpm-q2-widebody: A light, punchy widebody with big pop and drive pace. The catch: resets and drops run touchy.
pickleball.rpm-friction-pro-widebody: A soft, stable widebody with easy drops and a consistent sweet spot. The catch: power is mid-tier, below the elongated.
pickleball.six-zero-infinity-edgeless-black-diamond: An edgeless paddle with top-tier spin and very quick hands. The catch: low twist weight, so the sweet spot is less stable.
pickleball.six-zero-boulder-opal-14mm: A dense, muted paddle with a split on power. The catch: a small to average sweet spot.
pickleball.volair-shift-el: A heavy-hitting 14 mm elongated with real dwell and spin. The catch: it twists on off-center hits.
pickleball.pakle-fuse-elongated: A light, loud elongated with strong pop at a low price. The catch: stiff feel and touch shots need dialing in.

laptop.asus-zenbook-14-oled-um3406: A light 14-inch OLED laptop with long battery life on both Ryzen 7 8840HS and Ryzen AI 7 350 versions. The catch: the screens are 60Hz and measured dim at 360 to 387 nits.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t14s-gen-6: A light, slim ThinkPad with a well-liked keyboard and long battery life, especially on the Snapdragon model. The catch: the 1200p 60Hz IPS screen is plain, and Snapdragon models have app and game gaps.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m4: A fast, light 13-inch laptop with 16GB of RAM at a $999 starting price and all-day battery. The catch: the fanless body throttles under sustained heavy work.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g14-2025: Reviewers praise the light aluminum build and OLED screen with strong gaming speed for 14 inches. The catch: fans get loud and the body runs hot under load.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-x1-carbon-gen-13: A very light 14-inch Lunar Lake ThinkPad with a good OLED, a well-liked keyboard and longer battery life than the Gen 12. The catch: high price for modest multi-core speed.
laptop.alienware-18-area-51: A desktop-replacement 18-inch gaming laptop whose RTX 5090 version holds a full 175 W with cooling several reviewers call quiet for the class. The catch: it is very heavy and the battery is short.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m1: A silent fanless laptop that reviewers found fast for everyday work, with long battery life. The catch: it throttles under sustained heavy loads like video editing.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-15-m4: A large, light 15-inch Air praised for long battery life and quiet fanless running in everyday work. The catch: with no fan, it throttles or heats up under sustained heavy loads.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-15-m5: A large, fast, silent fanless 15-inch MacBook Air with long battery life that handles everyday work and light creative tasks well. The catch: it has a 60 Hz screen and few ports.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m4-pro-max: A fast, quiet 14-inch laptop with a bright mini-LED screen and long battery life, where the M4 Pro is enough for most buyers. The catch: memory and storage upgrades get expensive quickly.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m4: A base M4 MacBook Pro 14 with 16GB that reviewers praise for fast everyday work, long battery life and a good display. The catch: its single fan gets loud under heavy load.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m5: A 14-inch MacBook Pro with much faster SSD and GPU than the M4, a bright screen and strong battery life. The catch: it is a small upgrade for anyone already on an M4.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-16-m4-pro-max: A very fast 16-inch laptop for video editing and other creative work, with long battery life and mostly quiet fans. The catch: it is very expensive, especially RAM and storage upgrades.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-16-m5-pro-max: Fast, long-lasting laptop for heavy video, development and local AI work, with battery life that reviewers rate highly. The catch: it is expensive and weak for gaming.
laptop.asus-proart-px13-hn7306: A compact 13-inch convertible with strong CPU and GPU speed and a color accurate OLED touchscreen for creative work. The catch: the OLED is capped at 60Hz and fans get loud under load.
laptop.asus-rog-flow-z13-2025: A 13.4-inch tablet whose integrated graphics play demanding games at roughly RTX 4060 level. The catch: gaming battery life on the tested 32GB models is two hours at most, and prices start near $2,000.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-g16-2025: A fast gaming laptop with tool-free RAM and storage access and, on the higher-end configs, a 240Hz screen. The catch: battery life is short under gaming load.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-g18-2025: A fast 18-inch gaming laptop, tested with an RTX 5080, with a tool-free bottom panel. The catch: it weighs about 3.2 kg, so it suits desks more than travel.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-scar-18-2025: A fast 18 inch gaming laptop with a bright mini-LED screen and a tool-free bottom panel for upgrades. The catch: the RTX 5090 version is very expensive and battery life is short.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g14-2026: A compact 14-inch gaming laptop with a brighter OLED and strong gaming speed in the RTX 5070 Ti Intel versions reviewed. The catch: the price is high, and the fans get loud at full power.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g16-2025: A thin, light 16-inch gaming laptop with an OLED screen and speakers reviewers rate highly. The catch: RTX 5080 and 5090 versions are power limited and trail thicker laptops with the same GPU.
laptop.asus-tuf-gaming-a14-2025: A light 14-inch gaming laptop that runs cooler than the 2024 model and lasts long on battery in light use. The catch: its CPU is weaker in multi-core work than last year's.
laptop.asus-tuf-gaming-a16-2025: A 16-inch gaming laptop with strong game frame rates in the RTX 5050, 5060 and 5070 versions tested. The catch: several reviewers found the screen dim or short on brightness.
laptop.asus-vivobook-s-14-oled-s5406: A light 14-inch OLED laptop on Lunar Lake chips, with long battery life in several reviews. The catch: the 60Hz OLED screen is glossy and reflective.
laptop.asus-zenbook-a14-ux3407: The Snapdragon X versions reviewed are a very light 14-inch OLED laptop with battery life that lasts a full day or more. The catch: a 60Hz screen and weak graphics rule out gaming.
laptop.asus-zenbook-duo-2025: A 14-inch laptop with two OLED screens and a detachable keyboard that reviewers liked for multitasking and editing. The catch: battery life drops sharply with both screens on.
laptop.asus-zenbook-s-14-ux5406: A light x86 ultraportable with a 120Hz OLED, quiet fans and long battery life on the Lunar Lake Core Ultra models. The catch: multi-core speed trails many rivals.
laptop.hp-elitebook-x-g1i: A light 14-inch aluminium laptop for people who travel, with integrated graphics reviewers found fine for light video editing. The catch: multi-core CPU speed is modest on the Core Ultra 7 models reviewed.
laptop.lenovo-legion-5-gen-10: A light 15-inch gaming laptop with a bright 165Hz OLED screen. The catch: 8GB of VRAM on the RTX 5060 and 5070 versions limits demanding games and editing.
laptop.lenovo-legion-5i-gen-10: A compact gaming laptop with a praised OLED screen and strong performance for the price. The catch: battery life is short, about 3 to 5 hours of general use in three reviews.
laptop.lenovo-legion-pro-7i-gen-10: A 16-inch gaming laptop whose RTX 5080 version ranks among the fastest 5080 laptops reviewers tested, with a bright OLED. The catch: battery life is short and it needs a heavy 400 W charger.
laptop.lenovo-loq-15ahp10: A mid-tier 1080p gaming laptop with a well-liked keyboard and easy RAM and SSD upgrades. The catch: battery life is mostly short and the price is high unless it is on sale.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-e14-gen-7: A sturdy business 14-inch with a well-liked keyboard and upgradeable RAM and storage, suited to office work and students. The catch: the standard 60Hz screen is basic and low in color coverage.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-p1-gen-8: A light 16-inch workstation praised for its bright tandem OLED screen and its keyboard. The catch: reviewers call the price high, with tested configurations reported at about $3,500 to $4,169 and around €5,000.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-6: A business ThinkPad that reviewers praise for its keyboard, with long battery life on the Lunar Lake models. The catch: the basic IPS screen options look dull.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-x1-2-in-1-gen-10: A ThinkPad convertible with a well-liked keyboard and long battery life on the Core Ultra 7 258V version. The catch: it is expensive, and sustained multicore performance is limited.
laptop.lenovo-yoga-slim-7i-aura-edition: A Lunar Lake laptop that reviewers praise for long battery life, a good keyboard and cool, quiet running. The catch: multi-core speed trails rivals, and the IPS panel is not OLED.
laptop.microsoft-surface-pro-11-13: A Windows tablet on Snapdragon with quick everyday performance and battery life often around 12 hours in tests. The catch: some x86 apps and games run badly or not at all on Arm.
laptop.msi-vector-16-hx-ai-a2xw: A bulky 16-inch gaming laptop that reviewers mostly rate as strong RTX 5070 Ti or 5080 performance for the money. The catch: fans get very loud in the top performance modes.
laptop.razer-blade-14-2025: A thin, sturdy aluminum 14-inch gaming laptop with a 120Hz OLED that reviewers found capable for its size. The catch: RAM is soldered and the price is high.
laptop.alienware-16-area-51-aa16250: A heavy 16-inch desktop replacement with strong RTX 5080 performance, an optional Cherry MX keyboard reviewers like and three M.2 slots. The catch: short battery life and a weight over 7 lbs.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m2: A thin, fanless redesign with MagSafe, a 1080p webcam and a brighter screen. The catch: it throttles under sustained heavy loads, and it costs $200 more than the M1 Air.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m3: A light, fanless ultraportable with long battery life and enough speed for everyday work and light photo and video editing. The catch: only two USB-C ports, and the 8GB base RAM limits heavier work.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m5-2026: A fast, silent, fanless ultraportable with all-day battery and a strong keyboard, which reviewers say suits most people. The catch: the display is still 60Hz.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-15-m3: A large, light, fanless 15-inch MacBook Air that reviewers found silent and quick enough for everyday work. The catch: long, heavy loads such as video editing run slower than on a fan-cooled MacBook Pro.
laptop.apple-macbook-neo-2026: A budget aluminum MacBook with quick everyday performance, good battery life and a strong keyboard and trackpad. The catch: only 8GB of RAM, plus no keyboard backlight.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-13-m2: A 13-inch MacBook Pro with a clear M2 gain over the M1, a fan and long battery life. The catch: the old design and two ports make the MacBook Air M2 the better buy.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m1-pro-max: A fast 14-inch laptop with a mini-LED screen, MagSafe, HDMI and an SD slot, praised for video editing. The catch: launch pricing was high and some reviewers dislike the notch.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m5-pro-max: A fast, sturdy 14-inch laptop with strong CPU and GPU speed, and some reviewers say the M5 Pro is enough. The catch: it runs hot and throttles under heavy sustained load.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-16-m1-pro-max: A powerful 16-inch laptop that reviewers praise for video and photo editing, its mini LED screen and quiet cooling. The catch: it is heavy and has no USB-A port.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-16-m2-pro-max: A fast 16-inch laptop with a praised mini-LED screen and long battery life. The catch: it is only a modest step over the 2021 M1 Pro and M1 Max models.
laptop.asus-proart-p16-h7606: A light Windows creator laptop with strong editing performance and a color accurate OLED screen. The catch: the screen is limited to 60Hz.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-scar-16-2025: A fast desktop-replacement gaming laptop with a bright mini-LED screen and tool-free RAM and SSD access. The catch: it is heavy, needs a large charger, and battery life is short.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-scar-18-2024: An 18-inch gaming laptop with a bright mini-LED screen that reviewers rate highly. The catch: a plastic build and a high price for what it offers.
laptop.asus-rog-strix-scar-18-2026: An 18-inch RTX 5090 desktop replacement with a bright 4K mini-LED screen and tool-free upgrades. The catch: it is very heavy, very expensive and weak on battery.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g14-2024: A light 14-inch aluminum laptop with a well-liked OLED screen and speakers, aimed at people who want portable gaming and creative work. The catch: memory is soldered, so the RAM size bought is final.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g16-2024: A thin, light aluminium 16-inch gaming laptop with a 240Hz OLED screen and speakers that reviewers praise. The catch: the RAM is soldered, so buyers must choose the amount at purchase.
laptop.asus-rog-zephyrus-g16-2026: A thin 16-inch gaming laptop with a bright OLED, excellent speakers and much better battery life than last year's on RTX 5080 versions. The catch: a very high price, with last year's model cheaper.
laptop.asus-tuf-gaming-a16-2024: A 16-inch gaming laptop with a 165Hz screen and strong Ryzen 9 performance for the price. The catch: ports are limited and the top fan modes are loud.
laptop.asus-zenbook-14-oled-ux3405: A light 14-inch laptop with a vivid 120Hz OLED touchscreen and long battery life in several reviews. The catch: RAM is soldered, and fans get loud in performance modes.
laptop.asus-zenbook-s-16-um5606: A light, thin 16-inch laptop with a 3K 120Hz OLED and strong integrated AMD graphics. The catch: it gets warm under load, on the lap or underside.
laptop.dell-xps-14-2026-da14260: A thin aluminum 14-inch laptop with a well-liked OLED option and long battery life, especially on the IPS versions. The catch: the price is high, and ports are limited to USB-C.
laptop.dell-xps-16-2026-da16260: A slim, light 16-inch aluminum laptop with a sharp tandem OLED screen and integrated graphics that suit office and creative work. The catch: only three USB-C ports, with no HDMI or SD card reader.
laptop.hp-omnibook-ultra-14-snapdragon-x2-elite: A thin aluminum 14-inch Windows laptop with a sharp OLED and long battery life. The catch: a high price, few ports and weak gaming.
laptop.lenovo-chromebook-plus-14-gen-10: A fanless Chromebook Plus with a bright OLED screen and fast everyday performance on the Kompanio Ultra 910. The catch: limited ports, with only two USB-C, one USB-A and no HDMI.
laptop.lenovo-legion-5i-gen-9: A 16-inch gaming laptop that reviewers mostly found strong for the price, with a well-liked keyboard. The catch: fans get loud under heavy load.
laptop.lenovo-legion-7i-gen-9: A 16-inch gaming laptop with fast Core i9 and RTX 4070 performance, upgradeable RAM and a bright screen. The catch: battery life was short in several tests, around three hours or less.
laptop.lenovo-legion-pro-5i-gen-10: A fast 16-inch gaming laptop with a great keyboard and bright OLED screen. The catch: battery life is short, with reviewers measuring roughly three to five hours on several configs.
laptop.lenovo-legion-pro-7i-gen-9: A large 16-inch gaming laptop with top-tier performance across RTX 4080 and 4090 configs and a bright 240Hz screen. The catch: it is heavy and battery life is short.
laptop.lenovo-loq-15ahp9: A budget gaming laptop that reviewers found strong at 1080p in the Ryzen 7 8845HS and RTX 4060 config. The catch: fans get loud in performance mode and battery life is short.
laptop.lenovo-loq-15irx10: A budget gaming laptop with a good keyboard and upgradable RAM and storage. The catch: battery life is short, with reviewers reporting anywhere from under 1.5 hours of gaming to about 5 hours.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-e14-gen-6: A budget ThinkPad with a well-liked keyboard and upgradeable RAM and storage. The catch: the 1920x1200 screen has weak colour coverage, so it suits office work better than photo or video editing.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-e16-gen-1: A 16-inch office ThinkPad that reviewers mostly praise for its keyboard and its fit for everyday office work. The catch: the 1920 by 1200 screen is dim with weak colour coverage.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-l14-gen-5: A business ThinkPad with upgradeable RAM and a well-regarded keyboard. The catch: the standard screen does not cover full sRGB, so colour work needs the optional panel.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-p1-gen-7: A 16-inch ThinkPad workstation praised for its keyboard and haptic trackpad in a fairly thin body. The catch: it is expensive, with list prices that reviewers called high.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-p14s-gen-5: A ThinkPad workstation praised for its keyboard, user-upgradeable RAM and good 120Hz screen. The catch: fans get loud under load.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-5: A 14-inch business ThinkPad that reviewers praise for its keyboard, ports and upgradeable, repairable design. The catch: integrated graphics limit heavy editing and demanding games.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t14s-gen-5: A light, sturdy business ThinkPad that reviewers find fine for office work. The catch: performance is modest, and two reviewers say it is not suited to gaming.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-x1-2-in-1-gen-9: A light business convertible with a keyboard reviewers praise, aimed at corporate buyers. The catch: Core Ultra U-series speed is modest and the price is high for what it delivers.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-x1-carbon-gen-12: A light 14-inch business ultraportable that reviewers praise for its keyboard and OLED screen. The catch: the price is high, and several reviewers point to cheaper rivals or the Gen 11.
laptop.lenovo-yoga-9i-2-in-1-gen-9: A 14-inch convertible with a vivid OLED screen and well-liked speakers in a light metal body. The catch: there is no SD card reader, and integrated graphics limit it to light gaming.
laptop.lenovo-yoga-pro-9i-gen-9: A 16-inch laptop with a bright mini-LED screen, strong speakers and fast CPU and GPU power. The catch: battery life is modest, especially at high brightness.
laptop.microsoft-surface-laptop-13-inch-1st-edi: A 13-inch Windows on Arm laptop with long battery life and quiet running on the Snapdragon X Plus version. The catch: a 60Hz screen, and several reviewers favor the 13.8-inch Surface Laptop.
laptop.microsoft-surface-laptop-7-15: A 15-inch Windows on ARM laptop praised for long battery life on the Snapdragon X Elite model. The catch: some apps and games still do not run well on ARM.
laptop.msi-raider-18-hx-ai-a2xw: A big 18-inch desktop replacement with a bright 4K mini-LED screen and strong gaming and editing speed. The catch: it is heavy, the fans get loud under load, and it costs a lot.
laptop.razer-blade-14-2024: The RTX 4070 version is one of the fastest 14-inch gaming laptops, with a 140W GPU and upgradeable RAM. The catch: it costs up to $700 more than the 2024 Zephyrus G14.
laptop.razer-blade-16-2025: A thin, light 16-inch gaming laptop with an OLED screen and a better keyboard than last year's. The catch: RTX 5090 gains over the 4090 model are small and the price is very high.
laptop.samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-14: A solid-built 14-inch laptop with a bright 120Hz screen that reviewers mostly like. The catch: multicore performance is only average on the Core Ultra 256V and 226V models tested.
